# Md Sabbir Ahmed Khan (Sabbir Khan, "Rey")

> Senior Android Engineer, product builder and startup CTO with 12+ years of
> production experience. Kotlin, Jetpack Compose and Kotlin Multiplatform
> specialist. An AI-first developer: coding agents connected over MCP write the
> first drafts, and twelve years of production judgment decides what ships.
> Android is the specialism, not the ceiling — KMM delivers iOS from the same
> codebase, and agentic AI extends him to backend, web and release automation.
> Available worldwide — remote or relocation, working GMT+8.
> Three ways to engage: hire him for a senior/staff/lead Android role, hire him
> to build a product, or partner with him as your equity CTO.

## Who he is

- 12+ years shipping production Android applications, end to end.
- Founder of Power GP BD (2012–2018): 100+ Android apps shipped, two Facebook
  Startup Program awards. One app, Theatre, passed 500,000 Play Store downloads
  (it is no longer listed on the Play Store).
- At Kutumbita (2018–2019): designed and built Kinship.ai single-handedly, from
  architecture to Play Store release — a real-time workplace assistant putting HR
  self-service in the hands of garments-industry floor workers over Socket.io and
  Firebase Cloud Messaging (no longer listed on the Play Store).
- Lead Software Engineer II at Samsung R&D (2019–2022): Samsung Health, Wear OS
  companions syncing over BLE to Tizen watches, and feature work in the
  SmartThings iOS app.
- Led Android at Plentina (2022), a US fintech running Buy-Now-Pay-Later in the
  Philippines and Vietnam.
- At Avetics Global: owned the ground-up rewrite of two production Android apps,
  Volarious and V-Assist — multi-module architecture, Jetpack Compose, Hilt, and
  a real-time telemetry layer over custom TCP sockets, integrated with the DJI
  Mobile SDK — and set the architecture standards for a 6-person Android team.
- Selected by Google as a mentor for the Exchange with Google Developers pilot
  program (2021–2023); has trained 100+ developers across South and Southeast
  Asia, plus university and corporate teams.
- B.Sc. in Computer Science & Engineering, Ahsanullah University of Science and
  Technology.
- Languages: Bengali (native), English (professional).

  relocation. See https://reysabbir.com/projects/ and https://reysabbir.com/qa/.
- **Client product development** — you bring the idea, he designs, architects
  and ships it. Not Android-only: Kotlin Multiplatform delivers Android and iOS
  from one codebase, and agentic AI extends the same engineer to the backend, web
  and release automation — an all-in-one software solution rather than an app plus
  four more contractors. See https://reysabbir.com/how-i-work/.
- **Equity CTO / technical co-founder** — for non-technical founders with no
  funding yet: he takes the entire technical side of the company under
  contract, builds the MVP, and is compensated with a percentage plus company
  ownership when the round closes. See https://reysabbir.com/partner/.

## Case studies

- **Volarious & V-Assist — Real-Time Enterprise Android** (Avetics Global): Two Android products for Avetics Global, running side by side on the same rugged tablet: Volarious, the operator’s control app, and V-Assist, the companion for tethered-power operations. Between them it is the brief any serious Android app carries — authentication, a live telemetry dashboard, light and dark themes, device settings, a system overlay, error and recovery states, Play Store releases — with one twist that shapes every decision: the data arriving over the socket is a live aircraft, so late data is useless data.
  Role: Senior Android Engineer. I owned the ground-up architectural rewrite, built features across both apps, and set the engineering standards the 6-person Android team worked to.
  V-Assist on Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.volarious.vlinestatus
  https://reysabbir.com/projects/#avetics
- **Plentina — Buy Now, Pay Later** (GrowFolio (formerly Plentina), Feb 2022 – Nov 2022 · Remote (US)): A US fintech startup expanding BNPL credit access across the Philippines and Vietnam needed its Android app to move fast in two markets — with payment flows that simply cannot fail.
  Role: Led Android development of the Plentina BNPL app.
  https://reysabbir.com/projects/#plentina
- **Samsung Health & WearOS** (Samsung R&D Institute, Oct 2019 – Feb 2022 · Dhaka): Samsung’s consumer health ecosystem spans phones, wearables and servers. Health data has to stay consistent across all three — including watches running a completely different OS (Tizen).
  Role: Lead Software Engineer II. I built health-tracking Android applications and their WearOS companions inside Samsung’s consumer wellness product line, and contributed features to the SmartThings iOS app.
  https://reysabbir.com/projects/#samsung
- **Kinship.ai — Workplace Assistant for the Factory Floor** (Kutumbita, 2018 – 2019): Bangladesh’s garments industry employs hundreds of thousands of floor workers whose only route to HR is a queue and a paper form. Kinship.ai replaced it with a chat thread: ask the assistant a question, report a broken machine with a photo, apply for leave, check salary or attendance — in the moment, on the cheap Android phone already in their pocket.
  Role: I designed and built the Android app entirely on my own — architecture, implementation and Play Store release.
  https://reysabbir.com/projects/#kinship

## Public projects

- **Football Predictor 2026** — The bracket engine for FIFA’s new 48-team World Cup. FIFA’s 2026 format is new and genuinely hard: 48 teams, 12 groups, and a Round of 32 where third-placed qualifiers depend on results across every other group. I designed an engine that evaluates 450+ valid bracket combinations and recalculates the entire knockout tree in real time as you fill in results — following the official FIFA regulations to the letter. What takes analysts spreadsheets, the app does instantly, 100% offline.
  Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=xyz.androidrey.predictor
- **GitHub Client** — The “how I write code” exhibit — read the source. An open-source Android app I keep public for one reason: so you can see exactly how I structure production code. Multi-module clean architecture (app / features / common / network / storage / theme), unidirectional state, offline support, and real tests — not a toy repo.
  Source on GitHub: https://github.com/sabbirreyjohn/Github-Client · YouTube demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pzxTVq5kKnE

## Answers to the questions he is usually asked

### Walk me through a hard problem you solved recently.

On V-Assist, I owned a premium feature the company had already marketed: the drone scans a QR code from the air, tracks it in flight, and lands precisely on top of it — all driven from the Android-based DJI remote control.

Close to release, it was failing. At high image quality, QR scanning lagged behind the live feed, so the drone couldn’t follow the code in time to land. Most people would have dropped the image quality and shipped. Instead I debugged the pipeline line by line and found the real bottleneck: the video codec and rendering path, not the detection.

Working from the codec documentation, I rebalanced decoding and rendering so the feed kept its quality while scanning ran in real time. The feature shipped on schedule, the drone lands on the mark without crashing, and it’s live in production today. That’s my pattern: find the actual cause, don’t trade away the product.

### What work are you proudest of?

The one closest to my heart is Theatre, a multimedia app from my Power GP BD years that crossed 500,000 downloads on the Play Store (it’s no longer live). Half a million people choosing something you built — that feeling never gets old.

The most recent one is Football Predictor 2026. FIFA’s new 48-team format is algorithmically nasty: the Round of 32 depends on third-place results across all 12 groups, with 450+ valid bracket combinations. I built an engine that resolves the whole knockout tree in real time, by the letter of the FIFA regulations. It turned something that confuses everyone into something anyone can play with.

### Why should we hire you — or build with you?

Because I’m a bridge. I understand non-technical people — clients, founders, stakeholders — and translate what they actually want into technical decisions. Twelve-plus years of shipping end to end means I don’t just write code; I architect, build, release and maintain.

Two more things I bring everywhere: I automate redundant work instead of tolerating it, and I stay calm under critical deadline pressure — finding the smart solution rather than the heroic all-nighter. Ask my last three teams about release week.

### You use AI heavily. How do you keep the engineering rigorous?

Simple rule: I decide, AI executes. Architecture, tech stack and library choices are mine. Coding agents accelerate the implementation — but I track exactly what they’re using, steer them away from the wrong library toward the right one, and shape the solution so it stays future-proof: fewer bugs, less repair work later.

I keep myself current with cutting-edge tooling precisely so I can direct it. The agents work to my decisions, not the other way around. Every line that ships is a line I’ve reviewed and can defend.

### What are you looking for next?

Three doors are open. First, senior/staff/lead Android roles — remote, or on-site anywhere in the world; I’m ready to relocate for the right team. Second, product development for clients: you bring the idea, I build it. Third, equity-CTO partnerships: I take over the entire technical side of an early-stage startup for a percentage plus ownership when it raises.

The thread connecting all three is ownership. I do my best work when I’m accountable for outcomes, not just tickets — building products I stand behind, with the freedom to do it right.
